gaps.assertion: Elevated HbA1c is used to diagnose and monitor type 2 diabetes.
Fasting plasma glucose above diagnostic thresholds indicates T2D.
Insulin resistance is a core pathophysiologic feature of T2D.
Progressive β-cell dysfunction contributes to hyperglycemia in T2D.
Metformin is first-line pharmacotherapy for many adults with T2D.
SGLT2 inhibitors lower glucose and reduce cardiorenal risk in selected T2D patients.
GLP-1 receptor agonists improve glycemic control and weight in T2D.
Obesity is a major modifiable risk factor for incident T2D.
CGM time-in-range complements HbA1c for glycemic assessment in T2D.
Systemic glucocorticoids can worsen hyperglycemia and unmask diabetes.
Low-grade chronic inflammation is linked to insulin resistance (immuno-metabolic bridge).
TNF-α signalling can impair insulin action in metabolic tissues.
Circulating IL-6 is associated with T2D risk and inflammatory tone.
hs-CRP is a clinical marker of systemic inflammatory burden.
Adipose tissue macrophage infiltration associates with insulin resistance.
NLRP3 inflammasome activation contributes to metabolic inflammation.
T2D is associated with increased susceptibility to certain infections.
Sustained hyperglycemia can impair aspects of innate immune function.
Some autoimmune conditions co-occur with higher T2D risk (bridge shortlist).
IL-1 pathway blockade has been studied for metabolic inflammation (research only).
PD-1 signalling contributes to T-cell exhaustion phenotypes (educational graph).
Immune checkpoint therapy is associated with immune-related adverse events.
Some irAEs and steroid treatment can present with hyperglycemia (bridge-relevant).
Islet autoantibodies mark autoimmune β-cell targeting in T1D (contrast with T2D).
LADA can present with adult-onset diabetes phenotypes overlapping T2D clinics.
TNF-α contributes to synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis (scope-locked pathway seed — not a partner-signed lock).
Anti-CCP (ACPA) antibodies are a serologic biomarker used in rheumatoid arthritis workup (scope-locked — not partner-signed / not CDS).
Anti-TNF therapy (e.g. infliximab class) improves clinical outcomes in rheumatoid arthritis when combined with methotrexate in established trials (scope-locked — response heterogeneity remains open).
IL-6 pathway signalling contributes to rheumatoid arthritis inflammatory tone (competing axis vs TNF-centric framing).
Some patients with inadequate anti-TNF response still show benefit from IL-6 pathway inhibition — supporting competing mechanisms for response heterogeneity (uncertain grade).
Macrophages are a cellular source of TNF-α — relevant to synovial TNF biology in rheumatoid arthritis (entity-slice seed).
Development of anti-infliximab antibodies is associated with reduced clinical response to infliximab in rheumatoid arthritis (immunogenicity competing frame for anti-TNF response heterogeneity).

Low early trough infliximab levels and subsequent anti-infliximab antibodies associate with infusion reactions and treatment failure — supporting immunogenicity monitoring as a response-heterogeneity axis (not CDS).

RF and/or anti-CCP positivity has been associated with differential mean DAS28 improvement on anti-TNF therapy in observational cohorts (serology competing frame — direction and magnitude remain contested).
Pooled evidence does not support RF or anti-CCP status as a reliable predictor of clinical response to anti-TNFα agents (competing with single-cohort serology associations).
Rheumatoid factor is a serologic biomarker used in rheumatoid arthritis classification and workup alongside ACPA (scope-locked LOINC marker — not an anti-TNF response predictor by itself).

Infliximab plus methotrexate improves clinical and radiographic outcomes versus methotrexate alone in RA — relevant background for interpreting anti-TNF response and immunogenicity in combination regimens.
Type I interferon pathway activation associates with SLE pathophysiology (illustrative — not locked pilot).
ANA testing is used in the serologic workup of SLE (illustrative biomarker — not locked pilot / not CDS).
IL-17 pathway signalling drives psoriatic skin inflammation (illustrative — not locked pilot).
IL-23 pathway biology associates with IBD inflammatory tone (illustrative — not locked pilot).
Circulating follicular helper T cells are increased in systemic sclerosis (dual-track PRD MVP seed — not Stage 1 partner lock; not CDS).
Tfh cells produce / drive IL-21 as a defining helper cytokine for B-cell help (foundational Tfh biology; used as SSc pathway axis context).
IL-21 induces differentiation of human naive and memory B cells into antibody-secreting plasma cells (B-help axis underpinning SSc Tfh–IL-21 framing).
In systemic sclerosis, circulating Tfh promote plasmablast differentiation through the IL-21 pathway (SSc-specific pathway seed).
T follicular helper-like cells contribute to skin fibrosis (fibrosis-facing competing / complementary frame for SSc pathway exploration).
Imbalance toward Tfh1 cells is associated with aberrant B-cell differentiation in systemic sclerosis (competing Tfh-subset explanation).
EBV infection has been hypothesized to contribute to scleroderma fibroblast / TLR pathway dysregulation — separate uncertainty branch; not a proven Tfh→B→IL-21 causal merge.
Commentary frame: T follicular helper cells are discussed as drivers of skin fibrosis (neighbourhood support for the Taylor 2018 fibrosis-facing explanation).
In systemic sclerosis, peripheral CD21low B cells and serum IL-4 / IL-21 are reported to influence joint involvement (B-cell–IL-21 neighbourhood deepen; not Stage 1 RA lock).
Single-cell analysis of SSc skin identifies a CXCL13+ Tfh-like T-cell cluster adjacent to B cells and poised to promote local B-cell responses (neighbourhood deepen; not Stage 1 RA lock).
Serum BAFF is elevated in systemic sclerosis with enhanced BAFF signalling reported in SSc B lymphocytes (B-survival neighbourhood deepen; not a therapeutic claim).
BAFF antagonism attenuates skin fibrosis in the tight-skin mouse model (hypothesized translational frame — not human dosing, not CDS, not partnerSigned).

CXCL4 is a predominant protein secreted by plasmacytoid dendritic cells in systemic sclerosis and circulating levels associate with fibrosis phenotypes (biomarker neighbourhood — not a therapeutic claim).

Therapeutic IL-6 blockade can reverse TGF-β pathway activation signatures in dermal fibroblasts in SSc clinical-trial biospecimens (faSScinate insight — hypothesized translational frame; not dosing CDS).

B-cell depletion with rituximab has been studied in diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis with exploratory clinical and skin signals (small open-label / pilot neighbourhood — hypothesized only; not approved SSc CDS).
Indigenous Clostridium clusters IV and XIVa promote accumulation of colonic Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (mouse gut–immune neighbourhood seed — not CDS; not Stage 1 RA lock).
A rationally selected mixture of human microbiota Clostridia strains induces Treg abundance and anti-inflammatory programs in germ-free mouse models (gut–immune neighbourhood; not human CDS).
Commensal microbe-derived butyrate induces differentiation of colonic regulatory T cells (core SCFA ↔ mucosal Treg axis; mouse Nature 2013 evidence).
Microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids regulate size and function of the colonic Treg pool in an Ffar2 (GPR43)-dependent manner in mice (SCFA class ↔ mucosal Treg).
SCFAs can promote T-cell differentiation into IL-17-producing (Th17) cells depending on cytokine milieu via HDAC inhibition / mTOR–S6K (competing frame vs Th17 inhibition — hypothesized only).
Butyrate can inhibit Th17 differentiation (IL-17 / RORγt axis) while upregulating IL-10 in T-cell models of colitis induction (competing frame vs SCFA→Th17 promotion — hypothesized only).
Butyrate enhances intestinal barrier function by facilitating tight-junction assembly via AMPK activation in Caco-2 monolayers (barrier context for mucosal immune neighbourhood).
Activation of Gpr109a, receptor for niacin and the commensal metabolite butyrate, suppresses colonic inflammation (and carcinogenesis) in mouse models — receptor hop for SCFA mucosal neighbourhood.

Butyrate conditions human dendritic cells to prime IL-10-producing type-1 regulatory T cells via both HDAC inhibition and GPR109A signalling (human DC frame — hypothesized for therapeutic generalisation).
Metabolites produced by commensal bacteria promote peripheral regulatory T-cell generation (independent peripheral-Treg hop alongside colonic Treg seeds — mouse; not CDS).
The microbial metabolite butyrate regulates intestinal macrophage function via histone deacetylase inhibition (innate hop for SCFA mucosal neighbourhood — mouse).
Microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids crosstalk with intestinal epithelial HIF programmes that augment tissue barrier function (barrier deepen — mouse/mechanistic).

Electrical stimulation of the peripheral vagus nerve attenuates systemic inflammatory responses to endotoxin, including hepatic and serum TNF, in rodent endotoxaemia models (cholinergic anti-inflammatory neighbourhood — not CDS).

The inflammatory reflex frames a hard-wired autonomic (vagal cholinergic) pathway that reflexively monitors and adjusts acute inflammatory cytokine responses in real time (conceptual neighbourhood frame — not a disease cure claim).

The nicotinic acetylcholine receptor α7 subunit is required for acetylcholine- and vagus-mediated inhibition of macrophage TNF synthesis (essential receptor node of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway).
Vagus / nicotinic α7 signalling attenuates macrophage activation via Jak2–STAT3 phosphorylation in experimental inflammation (mechanism companion to α7 TNF inhibition).
Acetylcholine-producing memory-phenotype T cells relay vagus nerve signals required for inflammatory-reflex inhibition of macrophage TNF (neural → lymphoid → innate immune hop).

Implantable vagus nerve stimulation can modulate peripheral blood TNF production and RA clinical composite scores in small human pilot cohorts (hypothesized translational frame — not a settled clinical cure; not CDS).
Splenectomy inactivates the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway during lethal endotoxemia and polymicrobial sepsis — spleen as required effector organ for vagus-mediated TNF brake (rodent).
The splenic nerve is required for cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway control of TNF in endotoxemia (vagus → celiac/superior mesenteric → splenic nerve → spleen macrophage TNF brake).
Pharmacological stimulation of the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway attenuates systemic TNF responses (drug-pathway hop parallel to electrical VNS — rodent; not CDS).
Cholinergic neural signals to the spleen down-regulate leukocyte trafficking via CD11b (trafficking hop beyond TNF-only frames — rodent).
The cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway can inhibit tumor necrosis factor during ischemia–reperfusion injury (context expand beyond endotoxin — rodent; not clinical cure).
